Modelled from the working drawings (verkteikningar, Magnús Jensson teiknistofa, Aug–Nov 2025), with the bedroom moved up to the loft. Walls, openings, roof and heights follow the drawings. The interior fit-out is simplified and the terrain is an approximation of the site plan.

Skeleton view · sizes in mm Load-bearing studs (engineering drawings) Floor joists and ledgers Electrical points (TKM xx_16_02) · sockets, switches/boxes, lights Partitions – studs assumed 45×70 Stone wool between the studs of the outer walls and between the rafters Battens 34×45: across the rafters in the ceiling, and on the inside of the outer walls (installation void for cables and pipes) · rafters 45×245 c/c 600 (faint) Steel UNP-140, HEB-200 ridge · SHS-100 post Lengths of timber pieces (mm) appear on pieces within about 3.5 m of you. Arrow keys / W A S D move, Q / E down / up, Shift faster. Tape measure: point at a corner line, hold T, move to another line and let go · Backspace removes the last tape, X clears all. N hides / shows all the measurement numbers. Joist and stud spacing and sizes are from the drawings. Where each row starts is set out from the walls in the model – check on site.
Drag to orbit · right-drag to pan · scroll to zoom · arrow keys to move · Q/E down/up

Click the view to steer with the mouse · ↑ ↓ ← → or W A S D to walk · Shift to run · Esc frees the mouse

How to use the Hrafnsnes model

Open and close this help with the Help button or H; Esc closes it.

Looking around (normal view)

DragOrbit round the house
Right-dragPan sideways
Scroll / pinchZoom in and out
↑ ↓ ← → or W A S DMove forward, back, left, right
Q / E (or PgDn / PgUp)Move down / up
Hold ShiftMove faster

Walking and flying (first person)

Walk buttonsOutside, Ground floor, Loft bedroom put you inside the model at eye height; you walk on the floors and stairs and can't go through walls
Click the viewSteer with the mouse (the white dot in the middle is where you look); Esc frees the mouse again. Without that, drag to look round
↑ ↓ ← → / W A S DWalk; Shift runs
Skeleton viewsFly instead of walk: through walls, and Q / E go down / up
Exit walkBack to the normal orbit view

Views

Exterior – Approach, South, West, North, East, Aerial. Drawings – ground floor and loft plans and sections A–A and B–B, as in the architect's sheets. Skeleton – the framing: Overview, Centre wall, Floors from above.

Show switches

Roof · Loft & stair · FurnitureHide these to see inside
Room namesLabels for each room
Site & landscapeTerrain from ÍslandsDEM, gravel, car parks, road, cliffs and sea
Skeleton (framing)Studs, plates, joists, beams, battens and steel instead of finished walls
MetricsAll dimension lines, labels and timber lengths in the skeleton view (key N)
Electrical pointsSockets (boxes), switches and junction boxes (discs) and lights (crosses) from the TKM drawings, in the skeleton view
Corner linesThin outlines on every edge, so you can tell the pieces apart. Turns on by itself in the skeleton view
Bedroom door openSlides the loft bedroom door

Skeleton view – measuring

Hold TTape measure. Point at a corner line on a piece of timber and hold T – the line lights up yellow. Keep holding, move the mouse or the camera to another corner line; a red line shows the distance in mm. Let go of T and the tape stays
Two parallel lines give the square distance between them (gaps, sizes). The same line twice gives the length along it, snapping to the ends. Otherwise it is point to point
BackspaceRemove the last tape
XClear all tapes
NHide / show all the drawn measurement numbers (your tapes stay)
Timber lengthsThe small numbers on pieces appear on pieces within about 3.5 m of you

Cut, colours and environment

Section cutSlice the house from the south gable northwards
Plan cut heightSlice it horizontally, like a plan drawing
ColoursTry other colours for the ceiling, timber cladding and deck
Environment · SunDate and time (Iceland) – the sun, shadows and sky are calculated for the house's real position, including the equation of time and the light bending at the horizon. Below the horizon the lights come on
AnalemmaDots on a sky dome centred on you show where the sun stands at the chosen clock time on every other day of the year – the figure of eight. Solstices and equinoxes are labelled; the red ball is today
Stars, moon & planetsThe brightest stars (named ones labelled), the Plough, Cassiopeia, Orion, the Summer Triangle, Cygnus and Pegasus, plus the moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn, where they stand at the chosen date and time. Stars are faint in daylight and full once the sun is 12° down. Underneath: which bodies are above the horizon and the moon's phase
Moon & planet pathsEach body's track across the sky over the chosen date (only the part above the horizon)
Sun pathThe sun's track across the sky on the chosen date, with the hours marked. Under the switches: the time of solar noon and how far the sun is ahead of or behind the clock
